en: The Ritual Manual for the Mahāvaiśravaṇa-deva-rāja Dhāraṇī,
translated by Prajñākara. One fascicle.
Chapter One: On the Painting of Images. If there are good men or good women who receive and uphold this dhāraṇī, they must first paint an image.
When painting an image,
one must never use animal-hide glue within the pigments;
one should use only fragrant juices.
On the first day of the waxing moon, invite artisans to perform cleaning and bathing, observe the fast, and receive the eight precepts.
When entering or leaving [the ritual space], one must wear the three types of robes.
If one uses the toilet, one must immediately bathe with fragrant water.
Furthermore, do not concern yourself with the amount of manual labor involved;
simply take fine white cotton cloth.
If white cloth is unavailable, high-quality fine silk will also suffice.
One zhang and five chi.
Depict a Heavenly King,
his body adorned with armor made of the seven treasures and vajra.
His left hand holds a trident and his right hand rests upon his hip; according to another version, his left hand cradles a stūpa. Beneath his feet he treads upon three yakṣa-demons.
The central figure is named Pṛthivī-devī, also known as Nandikeśvara.
On the left is named Nīlāmbā;
on the right is named Vilambā.
The faces of these celestial kings are terrifying.
With a fierce form and wrathful eyes wide open, on his right side are painted the five princes along with their retinues of yakṣas and rākṣasas from the two families;
on his left side are painted the five *dharmacārinī* goddesses along with their wives and other attendants.
As explained extensively in the Great Sūtra.
Chapter Two: On Constructing the Maṇḍala. When one wishes to construct a maṇḍala, one should begin its construction on the first day of the waxing moon.
A square altar measuring eight cubits, or six cubits and eight inches,
should be prepared on a selected superior site by digging one *zhang* deep to remove bones,
shards, stones, and other such impure objects.
In another location, take pure earth and firmly compact it until it is level and even.
Once it has dried, take yellow earth and sift it finely;
then mix it with white sandalwood powder to form mud for the altar.
Having scraped and polished [the surface] until it resembles a mirror, take rice flour and dye it with five colors.
On the altar, delineate three enclosures;
in the center, paint a vajra-flame wheel—or according to another version, paint a flaming fire-gem with light radiating upward—and in each of the four corners, paint a cross-shaped *viśvavajra*.
In the center of the second courtyard, paint a fire-jewel (*agnimaṇi*) with flames issuing upward.
On the southeast side, paint a three-pronged trident; on the southwest side, paint a *kunta* spear.
Within the mouth of the vase, place a lotus flower.
In the northwest, paint a large conch shell.
In the third enclosure, paint a lion king on the eastern side and a nāga king on the southern side.
On the west face, paint the King of Peacocks;
on the north face, paint the Yakṣa King standing upon the ground with a staff.
Furthermore, place a vase of fragrant water at each of the four corners of the maṇḍala.
Place various light snacks, flowers, leaves, and so forth inside the mouth of the vessel.
Then, the mantra-practitioner shall bathe and don fresh, clean garments.
Before the image of the Heavenly King, he shall arrange various kinds of incense, flowers, food, and drink.
Having completed the offerings, recite the mantra over one hundred and eight *harītakī* fruits.
Reciting the mantra over each fruit, burn them entirely in the fire.
Immediately thereafter, deliver one ingot of gold every day.
He shall have no lack of anything for the mantra-reciter.
When he obtains gold,
he shall use it all on that very day to make offerings to the Triple Gem and to poor children.
Do not give rise to a mind of stinginess.
Chapter Three: On Establishing the Boundary.
When one wishes to establish a boundary, first recite the name of Mahāvairocana Buddha one hundred times.
Thereafter, one establishes the boundary and makes this great vow, saying: "I, [Name],
shall carry these five yakṣas upon my head."
Treading upon all the rākṣasas,
I look up and pay homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm,
as well as to Vajrapāṇi the Guhyaka, the Mārṣa, and all the various benevolent spirit-kings.
The celestial kings, the earth kings, the mountain forests, rivers, oceans, the sun and moon, the five planets, and the twenty-eight lunar mansions;
the Dharma King Yama, the generals of the five paths of rebirth, the Lord of Mount Tai, the Director of Destiny, and the Registrar.
Enemies, creditors, officials of the underworld, those on the path of karma, disease-demons, the *piśāca* king Viśvakarman,
the yakṣa generals of the five directions, the three celestial youths, the seven stars, the seven lunar mansions, and the deities of the sun and moon.
Nanda, Upananda, Varuṇa, and all the other great nāga kings have fully witnessed and verified this.
I, [Name], now desire to accomplish this dharma-gate of the great dhāraṇī with its divine efficacy.
"I only pray that all the worthy sages and holy ones above will protect, mindfully regard, and empower me.
May I swiftly attain accomplishment and cause all to rejoice. Thus one should offer this invocation three times.
Furthermore, separately invite the dragon kings of the five directions, the four great heavenly kings, and the deities and spirits of the twenty-eight divisions.
Furthermore, separately invite the yakṣa hosts of the five directions.
First, recite the heart mantra, which is as follows:

*vateṭa mahāmaharu uhu uhu rājñeṭe svāhā*. Reciting it twenty-one times, one immediately establishes the boundary (*sīmābandha*). When treating illnesses at a person's home, [one should proceed thus].
First, one must respectfully invite the yakṣas of the five directions:

the Yakṣa of the Blue Emperor of the East, three zhang and two chi in height, exhaling blue vapor from his mouth; [the Yakṣa of] the Red Emperor of the South; the White Emperor of the West; the Black Emperor of the North; and the Yellow Emperor of the Center, and so forth.
The height is likewise the same as that of the Blue Emperor (Cakravartin). He exhales his breath according to the directions, and with each exhalation, he invites his retinue.

Chapter Four: Hand Gestures (Mudrā) Section One: The Standing Body Gesture of the Yakṣa (Yakṣa-sthita-kāya-mudrā), Number One. To perform the Yakṣa standing body gesture: stand with the right leg straight, stepping firmly upon the ground with the left foot.
At a distance of about one cubit [from the body],
straighten the three fingers of the left hand and,
with the thumb, press upon the nail of the little finger while supporting the waist.
Pointing three fingers forward,
use the five fingers of the right hand to press against the face and assume an expression of wrath.
To delimit the boundary, circumambulate the altar to the right once.
For each mantra recited, the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ devayakṣa bandha bandha hā hā hā hā svāhā. Second, the Rākṣasa-body-invoking mudrā: join both palms together.
Hook the two little fingers together;
place the two thumbs side by side against each other and join the wrists;
move the index fingers back and forth.
3. The Yakṣa Hook Seal (Yakṣāṅkuśamudrā). The third [seal], the Yakṣa Hook Seal, is performed according to the previous body seal;
with the index finger of the right hand placed upon the third joint of the middle finger.
When one proceeds on the path while keeping the mind directed toward the right,
all yakṣas together with their retinues will be filled with joy and shall constantly provide protection for the mantra-practitioner.
4. The Yakṣa Fire-Wheel Mudrā. For the fourth, the Yakṣa Fire-Wheel Mudrā:
support the right index finger with the left hand, and support the left index finger with the right middle finger.
The two ring fingers are bent within the palms with their two joints facing each other;
the two thumbs and the two little fingers are held straight and upright, their tips touching one another.
Recite the Great Heart Mantra. 5.
The Yakṣa Body Seal, the fifth: this seal of the yakṣa body cures all demonic illnesses;
one should rely upon this body seal.
The *teṣuḷi* mudrā for you is identical to the *liṣṭa-kāya* (standing body) mudrā:
the two thumbs of both hands are bent into the palms,
and the two ring fingers press down upon the nails of the two thumbs.
The index, middle, and little fingers are held together straight upward with their tips touching.
With the two elbows positioned five inches from the breasts, one recites the Great Body Mantra (Mahākāya-dhāraṇī). 6.
The Seal of the King of Great Joy (Mahāpramuditendra-mudrā), the sixth: With the right hand, firmly grasp the left hand to form a staff.
Then he recited the mantra, saying:
*Namaḥ kīli kīli, kumāri, hūlū cālu svāhā*. When official affairs are urgent or when a person of high rank is enraged...
If one recites this mantra seven times, [the deity] will immediately be greatly delighted.
7. The Seal for Binding Great Ghosts (Mahābhūta-bandhana-mudrā), the seventh: Extend both thumbs straight upward.
Bend the left index finger and place it against the base of the left thumb;
tuck the tip of the right index finger slightly inside.

8. Āhāra-mudrā (Food Seal), eighth: The two middle fingers of both hands are bent down, and all the fingers are collectively flexed within the palms. Both thumbs are bent with their tips pointing downward.
The two index fingers are held straight and upright.
The two middle fingers are also held upright but slightly curved.
The two ring fingers and the two little fingers are both bent together within the palms.
9. The Tooth Seal (Dantamudrā), the ninth: With both hands, the two thumbs are held upright with their tips pointing upward.
The two middle fingers are held straight up.
The left index finger is held upright and slightly bent.
Bend the right index finger so it rests upon the left thumb.
Hold the two middle fingers upright with their tips approximately half an inch apart.
Bend both ring fingers and both little fingers together into the palm.
Chapter Five: On Protecting the Body. When one wishes to protect the body, one should also invoke the yakṣas of the five directions and the Great Wheel Vajra (Mahācakra-vajra).
One should then recite the Mahācakra-vajra Dhāraṇī twenty-one times.
Furthermore, recite the mantra of the Body of the Heavenly King twenty-one times.
Then, the protective body mantra (*kāyarakṣā-mantra*) is as follows:

*Namo ratnatrayāya | Namo vaiśravaṇāya mahārājāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ gagaśana śana kuru kuru mahārāja rakṣa māṃ sarvabandhanavimocaka svāhā.* By reciting this mantra twenty-one times, the rite for protecting the body is accomplished.

Chapter Six: The Chapter on the Vast Entreaty, Number Five. Homage to Vaiśravaṇa! Homage to Dhanada! To the one who bestows wealth (Dhanīśvara)! O Acala! O Aparimita! O Dhanīśvara! O Pramakāruṇika! To all sentient beings! To those who are joyful and powerful! [I,] named [insert name], entreat you, O Dhanamada! O Parayaca! O Sryamagaca! Svāhā! Having recited this mantra seven times:
Next, recite the root mantra.
When reciting the mantra,
one should first invoke the names and pay homage to the Triple Gem and the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa.
They are able to bestow wealth and goods so that the aspirations of all sentient beings are fulfilled;
they bring them all to accomplishment and grant them peace and happiness.
Furthermore, another version states that regarding the method of invocation: first, place [the object] upon the handle of a *dou* (a grain-measure).
Prior to this, burn *guggulu* incense.
The practitioner should sit in the center of the ritual space with a focused mind.
Facing the sluice gate and wearing black robes,
recite the mantra seven times while calling out the name of the ghost or spirit once for each repetition;
that is, recite the mantra once and call the name of the ghost or spirit once for every single recitation.
Recite this up to forty-nine times.
In this manner, for seven days and seven nights,
beginning from the fifteenth day of the month until the twenty-ninth day, one should bathe with purity and observe the fast.
On the altar, burn agalloch incense and light seven lamps.
Outside, place a basin of pure water and perform the ritual;
the spirit will immediately manifest and may be spoken with at will.
Each ghost, having declared its own capabilities,
was recorded according to its words— its name, rank, and the tasks for which it was to be employed—
as well as all its wealth, such as gold, silver, and the seven treasures, along with its clothing.
As well as medicinal herbs, oceans, precious mountain treasures, celestial palaces, and dragon palaces;
all noble objects found in the Five Peaks and Four Rivers;
and all rare and extraordinary fruits found among humanity.
Furthermore, regarding the methods for incantations and rituals in the *Guhyagarbha-tantra-śāstra*, whatever one desires may all be brought forth without any hindrance.
Chapter Six: On Summoning Messengers. Now, when one wishes to dispatch spirits and deities as messengers:
First, one must separately prepare a station outside the mandala;
having placed a single lamp, a basin of pure water,
and a bundle of pure grass upon the ground, [one should proceed].
He prepared forty oil cakes and forty-nine oil-less cakes,
scattering them upon the grass.
One should call out the names of the various spirits and deities and offer them food;
only then can one command these gods and ghosts.
If one wishes to extensively recite the various sūtras and śāstras of the Tripiṭaka, [one must do so with this preliminary practice].
He immediately called for the recitation messengers;
if there were those who wished to engage in debate,
he then summoned the debate messengers.
If one seeks someone of keen intelligence and wisdom,
one should summon a messenger who is clever and highly intelligent;
if one seeks hidden treasures buried within the earth, [one should summon the appropriate deity].

If one seeks to enter the mountains to practice seated meditation, or to engage in alchemical flight and study the arts of the immortals, one should immediately call upon the messenger of the hidden treasures (vasudhāra-pālaka). If one seeks to perform the aforementioned rites,
one should immediately call upon the messenger of the former dharma.
If one desires the treasures of the dragon palaces,
one should immediately summon the messengers of the dragon palaces.
If one seeks the methods for invisibility, ascending to celestial palaces, and miraculous transformations, [one should likewise summon them].
One should immediately summon the spirit of invisibility.
If one seeks the dhāraṇīs for subjugating spirits and deities, or the methods for treading upon boiling water and restraining fire,
one should immediately summon the spirit of subjugation.
If one seeks food, drink, wealth, clothing, or marvelous formulas;
if one desires extensive knowledge;
or if one desires to seek victory.
If one seeks to engage in business for profit,
or if one seeks to cultivate fields with great expectations for gain;
If one seeks high office or seeks wealth and nobility,
one should then summon the Messenger of the Right Office of Destiny.
If one wishes to know whether a person will die or not,
one should immediately summon the Left Officer of Destiny (Zuósìmìng).
If one seeks to stabilize the residence, ward off calamities, suppress misfortune through prayers, and turn the ominous into the auspicious, [one should likewise summon him].
If one wishes to summon the messenger of the Northern Dipper,
or if one wishes to know the auspiciousness or misfortune of the records of the hells,
one should immediately summon the messengers of the Five Officials.
If one seeks long life and immortality,
one should summon the messengers of Mount Tai.
If one wishes to move mountains and uproot the seas, [one should likewise summon them].

If one wishes to know the minds of others or the intentions of spirits and deities, one should immediately summon the Vajra-messenger. If one wishes to know the minds of others and the intentions of spirits and deities,
one should immediately summon the Superknowledges-messenger.
If one seeks water, fire, swords, arrows, or poisons that cannot cause harm,
one should invoke the Seated Deity (Āsana-deva) and his messengers.
If one seeks to be beloved by all people, [one should likewise invoke them].
If one seeks to become a great sovereign physician, one should immediately summon the messenger of many spirits; if one seeks to become a sovereign of the divine mountains,
one should immediately summon the messenger of the sacred mountain.
If one seeks for the fragrance to pervade and perfume the entire body,
one should invoke the messenger of the King of Incense.
If one seeks to ride upon supernatural powers to travel through the ten directions, [one should likewise invoke him].
If one seeks to subdue evil māras, one should immediately invoke the messenger Īśvara; if one seeks great power,
one should immediately invoke the messenger Mahābala.
If one seeks to subdue an enemy,
one should invoke the Vrata-dhara messengers. When invoking them,
one should call upon whichever of the twenty-eight types of messengers listed above is appropriate.
This general invocation for the dhāraṇī is as follows:
Namo buddha-dhāraṇī,
namo dharma-dhāraṇī.
Namo saṃghanī, namo sarvamahākāla.

Hā hā rāja, protect and assist me! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ | Oṃ viśvamanaya deva-rāja dhāraṇī-saṃgraha sarva-mahā-vidyā-rāja-deva-rāja rakṣa māṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ | Oṃ ārya-vairocani-spharaṇa-dhāraṇī hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ | Oṃ mahā-vidyā-rāja-dhāraṇī-saṃgraha hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ.

The *Tīrthakararāja-dhāraṇī-saṃgraha*: Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ | Gopana-ga-ṛṣi-graha-rāja-nara-graha-rāja-saṃgraha | Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ | Oṃ | The *Mahābala-senāpati-dhāraṇī-saṃgraha*:
Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ | Jie jie | Oṃ | Yakṣa-graha-rāja-cic cic cic cic | Oṃ | Rākṣasa-graha-rāja-huan huan huan huan | Oṃ | Sarva-mahābala...
Halahā deva halaja, protect me and assist me in my service! Dhāraṇī-saṃgraha-dhāraṇī! If you do not comply, your head shall be split into seven pieces! Svāhā!
If one recites each of the nine dharanis of the aforementioned paths twenty-one times,
none of those twenty-eight types of messengers will fail to arrive.
When summoning ghosts and spirits,
one must wait for the darkness of night;
outside the altar, place pure grass spread upon the ground.
Along with a basin of pure water,
forty-nine oil cakes,
and forty-nine oil-free cakes.
After offering various types of cakes and other foods,
one should enter the maṇḍala and recite the mantra; if one encounters spirits or deities,
one must make a solemn vow.
Then, write down their names on a slip of food so that they may be summoned by calling them. Chapter Seven:

The Chapter on Reciting the Mantra of the Heavenly Kings. The *Vaiśravaṇa-deva-rāja-japta-dhāraṇī*: Oṃ samanta-buddhānāṃ vaiśravaṇāya svāhā. If one recites this mantra twenty-one times, all that is sought shall be fully accomplished.
Furthermore, there is the Root Seal:
interlace the two hands with the right hand over the left,
and extend the two ring fingers so that their tips meet.
Bend the two index fingers like hooks.
When inviting [deities], beckon toward oneself;
when dispatching them, wave outward.
When performing the recitation, form the mudrā at the heart and recite [the mantra] seven times; then, disperse the mudrā over the crown of the head and take up the rosary.
With single-minded concentration, recite the mantra.
Furthermore, there is another mantra of the True Mind:
Oṃ jvala śāntadhārāya svāhā. If one recites this mantra, all great vows will be fulfilled, and all worthy sages and saints will be greatly delighted.
Furthermore, the mantra of the Body of the Heavenly King is spoken as follows:

*Namo mahāśriyāya* (1) *namo vaiśramaṇāya* (2) *mahāyakṣasenāpataye* (3) *tadyathā* (4) *oṃ* (5) *śve svāhā* (6) *śve svāhā* | *śyenamati svāhā* | *śyāmatri svāhā* | *jaya-patiri-śreṣṭha svāhā* || If one recites this mantra one hundred thousand times and thereafter recites it for three additional days, one will achieve accomplishment.
Furthermore, when performing the ritual,
whether on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon or the fifteenth day of the waning moon,
one should do so in a pure chamber or an open space.
The image of the Heavenly King faces south;
the mantra-practitioner sits facing north,
burning incense of kunduruka and making offerings of milk porridge.
If one recites this for three nights, completing one thousand and eighty repetitions,
the Heavenly King will immediately manifest his form.
Whatever is sought shall be fulfilled, and its blessings and rewards will be inexhaustible.
If any messengers should come, do not be alarmed or afraid.
If there is anyone who can constantly recite this mantra before the image of the Heavenly King,
the Four Great Heavenly Kings will never leave their side.
Alternatively, if one dreams of sitting and conversing with a person of high rank,
this is a sign that the Heavenly King is bestowing protection upon the mantra-practitioner.
At that time, the practitioner should immediately make a great vow before an image of the Heavenly King and burn agalloch incense.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times;
whatever you seek will be accomplished according to your heart's desire without exception.
The mantra of the messenger is as follows:
Namo Vaiśravaṇāya mahāyakṣasenāpataye oṃ sarvakaraṇa-viśuddhane svāhā. If one seeks a person of high status, one should recollect [this mantra].
If one wishes for all sought-after matters to be fulfilled according to one's intent,
one should recite this mantra one thousand and eighty times; then,
within a dream, the celestial king’s messenger will appear.
The mantra master shall clearly recite it all into the ear.
Furthermore, one must form a hand-seal (mudrā):
having extended the index finger of the left hand upright, [proceed as follows].
Bend the four fingers down into the palm and press the upper joint of the thumb against the nail.
Place it at the side of the right ear and recite the mantra fifty-four times.
The left ear is likewise.
Furthermore, the mantra for the yakṣī messenger is spoken as follows:
Oṃ yakṣiṇī nārāyaṇī svāhā. If one performs offerings to this messenger as well, [the results will be attained].
All essential matters shall be accomplished.
Next, the Great Heart Mantra of the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa is proclaimed as follows:

*Ātakhru Vajrāya Viśvānaryakṣa Vāmaliye Vaśanaprabhāvanāya Himapaṃprasāya Tadyathā Trili Nisili Viśālamānāya Mahārājāya Khagagatamukha Svāhā.* If there be anyone who upholds and recites this mantra, [all their goals shall be fulfilled].
Every day at dawn, chew on a willow branch (*dantakāṣṭha*).
Then, begin the recitation and perform the altar offerings as previously described.
If one completes one hundred thousand recitations of this mantra, the Heavenly King will manifest his own form.
When one beholds the Heavenly King,
one should immediately take the food and drink from the altar to make offerings to the Heavenly King;
then, whatever aspirations the practitioner seeks shall all be fulfilled.
If the practitioner does not see the Heavenly King,
a voice will immediately sound from the midst of the void, saying:
"You need only recite the mantra with a diligent mind."
I shall fulfill that which you seek.
Whether there be a great wind or merely black clouds arise,
this rite shall likewise be accomplished.
If the aforementioned signs of success do not appear, recite the mantra seven additional times;
if you are then able to bind the person, the rite of this mantra will certainly be accomplished.
Furthermore, the Heart Mantra is spoken as follows:
Oṃ (1) kiṇi kiṇi (2) sarvakāryaśātanī (3) kṣiṇi kṣiṇi (4) ārakṣamīnaśaye (5) tribhūśri (6) vaiśramaṇāya svāhā. If there is anyone who constantly recites this mantra:
All things sought shall be swiftly accomplished.
The Heart-within-the-Heart Mantra is as follows:

Oṃ (1) Vīrakāya (2) Trailokya (3) Mārjaya (4) Sarvaduṣṭān (5) Sarvabandhān (6) Sambhara (7) Abhimukhi (8) Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā (9). If there is anyone who constantly recites this mantra, the Heavenly Kings will not depart from the mantra-practitioner and will protect them.
Next, the mantra for subduing Māra is spoken as follows:
Namo 'tine namo litāya.
Namo Dāritāya.
Namo le-le-le-le-le.

I respectfully entreat the Four Great Heavenly Kings, each leading eighty-four thousand forest deities. If there are evil persons, evil spirits, evil ghosts, celestial māras, terrestrial māras, or nāga-māras who disturb and harass this disciple, hold fast to "Le," Namo Le! Ghost!
Namo Śūraṅgama-samādhi! For me, bind the ghosts! Five desires, five precepts, Dharma-patience! Mulabaddha mulabaddha! Quickly, quickly, quickly, quickly!
As per the ritual command!
Namo Buddhāya! Namo Dharmāya!
Namo saṃghāya tadyathā oṃ.
Eṅgali eṅgale rikṣa kṣa kṣa.

*Chuo chuo chuo chuo nie chang le zai zai zai zai zai bo lu jie ti she po he.* Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times, and all evil Māras and malevolent spirits will be bound; there shall be none who do not submit. It should not be used for minor matters.
Chapter Eight: Seeking All Benefits. If one seeks to win the affection of a king, one should take one hundred and eight small red beans.
For each bead, recite the mantra once while burning it in the fire one hundred and eight times.
Then, the Great King shall dispatch a messenger to summon the mantra-master, arriving as swiftly as a flying arrow.
If one seeks a high official position or wishes to be respected by others,
take one hundred and eight grains of white mustard seed;
recite the mantra over each grain once and burn them in the fire until all one hundred and eight grains have been consumed.
Then the high official will revere [the practitioner] as if he were a Buddha and be greatly delighted.
If one seeks for the women of the high official’s household to come and pay homage,
one should take soil from an anthill and mix it with sandalwood-scented water.
Make one hundred and eight pellets of clay;
for each pellet, recite a mantra once and burn it in the fire until all one hundred and eight have been completed.
Immediately, someone from that household will come to question the mantra-reciter.
Whatever may be required, if there is anything needed, it shall certainly not be withheld or begrudged.
At times, the practitioner himself shall come to pay homage to the mantra-master;
even when the mantra-master is not present, he shall constantly keep him in mind with devotion.
If one seeks to be honored by all households,
one should take one hundred and eight seeds of the *nimba* tree;
reciting the mantra over each seed once, one should burn them in fire for one hundred and eight times.
Then all the households will come to pay their respects to the mantra-practitioner as if to their own parents;
whatever they wish for in their hearts shall be fulfilled without fail.
If one wishes to subdue an enemy,
take the root of *achyranthes aspera* (changpu) and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times; having finished,
rub it upon one's own face and mouth, and hold it in the mouth.
There are no enemies who will not submit to it.
If there are wicked people who harass the mantra-practitioner,
he should mentally visualize the form of the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa.
Recite the mantra once;
before it is completed, that evil person will be unable to move.
If one wishes to release them, [recite the mantra again].
He immediately forms the thought of relinquishing [the enmity],
and that person returns to his former state of normalcy.
If one does not wish for an enemy to dwell in the same village or neighborhood, [one should practice this].
Alternatively, one may take one hundred and eight stakes of *kaṭuka* wood;
for each stake, recite the mantra once and burn it in the fire one hundred and eight times until they are exhausted.
Then, that evil person will be unable to remain.
If one seeks the great joy and protection of the devas,
one should take ghee, honey, and fruits,
recite the mantra over them one hundred and eight times, and burn them in fire.
Then all the devas were greatly delighted.
When one wishes to travel a long distance,
one should recite the mantra over a staff made of grain-wood and then proceed.
One will find peace in all difficult circumstances and remain free from obstacles.
If one seeks to be loved and respected by all people,
one should recite the mantra over a handful of sesame seeds.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and burn it in fire;
all people will come to revere you.
If you wish to enter the mountains to avoid all evil birds and beasts as well as various wicked bandits, [perform this].
Take one hundred and eight grains of white mustard seed.
Recite the mantra over each grain once, then burn them in fire or scatter them among the mountains;
all evil birds and beasts will then hide away.
Furthermore, all evil and contemptible beings will be unable to lift their heads.
If one wishes to seek rain,
take one hundred and eight apricot kernels.
Recite the mantra over each bead twenty-one times;
as soon as this is completed, cast it into the waters of a dragon pond, and rain will fall immediately.
If one seeks to stop the rain:
Recite the mantra over a handful of *wuzi* (walnuts) and burn them in fire;
the rain will immediately cease.
When one wishes to go begging for food:
First, recite the mantra over the alms bowl one hundred and eight times.
To whatever place one goes, all food and drink will be spontaneously obtained;
if there is anything else remaining, it will naturally vanish.
If one wishes to eat again, one should immediately recite the mantra once with a sincere mind toward the bowl,
and all food and drink will once more become full as before.
If one seeks to behold the goddess Puṇyavatī, [one should proceed as follows].
One should fast for one day and one night,
burn *sugandhaka* incense before the Buddha,
and recite the mantra over one hundred and eight white flowers, scattering them before the Buddha.
The goddess Śrī appeared before him;
whatever wealth, treasures, and all other matters the mantra-practitioner sought were all obtained according to his heart's desire.
If one seeks to avoid all ghosts and spirits,
take a handful of white mustard seeds and ghee; for each seed,
recite the mantra once, and when one hundred and eight repetitions are complete, burn them in fire.
There are no malevolent spirits that will not be subdued.
If there are wicked people who give rise to unwholesome thoughts toward the Triple Gem and repeatedly come to harass and disturb them, [they shall likewise be overcome].
Recite the mantra twenty-one times over your own hand;
then, while calling out the name of that wicked person, strike their body from afar.
That person will immediately give rise to a virtuous mind and will certainly not come to cause further trouble or disturbance.
If one wishes to rectify this, the mantra master should give rise to a mind of compassion;
by reciting [the mantra] once before that wicked person, they will return to their former state as usual.
If one wishes to subdue a wicked person...
If one recites the mantra over ghee and curd one hundred and eight times and burns them in the fire,
that wicked person will immediately give rise to a mind of reverence.
If one wishes to seek the reverence of all people, [one should do this].
Recite the earth-taking mantra twenty-one times and scatter it over one’s own body;
all who see this will not fail to regard one with reverence and admiration.
If one wishes to seek great majesty and power, [one should do so].
If one applies mantra-ink upon the forehead,
all who see it will not fail to feel respect and affection.
If one seeks great merit and virtue, people will come to show him reverence.
One should take ashes and recite the mantra over them twenty-one times;
by smearing these upon one's own body and entering the great assembly,
all who see one will be filled with joy.
If one seeks to travel a long distance and wishes not to be harmed by wild beasts,
one should recite the mantra over one's own left hand;
form a fist by digging the four fingers into the thumb.
First, there is no hindrance.
If one wishes to know which boy or girl is afflicted by a yakṣa-demon illness,
one should fashion the form of a yakṣa out of clay.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times before a mirror.
When asked, the person possessed by a spirit or the patient will immediately speak the names of the deities or ghosts.
If there is anyone afflicted by *gudu* (poisonous sorcery), [the same applies].
If one recites the mantra over water twenty-one times, the venomous insects will immediately emerge of their own accord.
If there is someone suffering from a demonic illness,
one should recite the mantra over five-colored thread twenty-one times and tie it into twenty-one knots.
If it is tied around the neck of a sick person, their illness will be immediately cured.
If there is one suffering from heart pain, take pomegranate juice and recite the mantra over it twenty-one times; give it to the patient to drink, and the illness will be immediately cured.
Alternatively, by reciting mantras over a branch of a pomegranate tree and striking the patient with it, they will also recover.
Or, by applying yellow earth to the heart center, they will immediately recover.
This applies even if one suffers from the disease of a wild fox.
Recite the mantra over five-colored threads and have a young girl twist them together.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and tie them around the patient's neck;
recite it once more, and if you strike the patient with a willow branch, they will immediately recover.
If one suffers from ailments of the waist or the joints,
take a bowl of pure water and a blade of bin-iron,
and empower them by reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
If one applies it to the site of pain, one will immediately recover.
If one seeks protection for oneself and one's companions,
take white mustard seeds, ashes, and water.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times and scatter it in the four directions;
immediately, one will protect oneself and one's companions, and all shall attain peace and happiness.
If one wishes to seek a cure for swellings or abscesses:
Recite the mantra over white sandalwood one hundred and eight times;
apply it to the swelling and it will be cured.
If there is pain in the head or in half the body, [apply it likewise].
Recite the mantra over twenty-one times over ghee or sesame oil;
by applying it to the painful area, one will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, there is another method for those suffering from swellings.
Before a stūpa containing relics,
recite the mantra over pomegranate sap and sandalwood one hundred and eight times,
and apply it to the swelling.
He will immediately recover.
If there is one suffering from wind-disorders of the ear,
one should consecrate ghee with the mantra twenty-one times.
If one gives food to a sick person, they will immediately recover.
If someone suffers from a disease of the head or crown,
reciting the mantra over realgar (*haritaki*) thirty-seven times and applying it to the painful area will cause immediate recovery.
If anyone suffers from red eyes,
they should recite the mantra over twenty-one pieces of rhubarb and apply them to their forehead;
they will then be cured immediately.
If a person suffers from a wind-disorder (vāta-roga),
one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over powdered *śrīkhaṇḍa* (blue sandalwood) and drink it mixed with water;
they will be cured immediately.
If a person suffers from sores, scabies, or ringworm,
one should recite the mantra over powdered *kaliṅga* twenty-one times,
mix it with oil, and apply it to the afflicted area; they will then be healed immediately.
If a person suffers from an infectious fever or malaria,
one should recite the mantra over twenty-one willow twigs;
by having the patient hold them while walking, they will immediately recover.
If a person is bitten by a snake,
after the incantation is completed, scatter [the ashes] thirty-seven times over the site of the bite;
it will be cured immediately upon application.
If a person is stung by a scorpion, one should recite the mantra over dried meat and burn it in fire; applying the ashes to the afflicted area will immediately eliminate the ailment.
If there is a woman suffering from a swelling of the breast, [the same shall be applied].
If one recites the mantra over sesame seeds twenty-one times and applies them to the painful area, the pain will be immediately relieved.
If a woman suffers from menorrhagia or leukorrhea, she should recite the mantra over scented water twenty-one times and drink it; she will then be cured.

If a person suddenly suffers from demonic possession, speaking deliriously, or running about in madness, one should empower water with this mantra twenty-one times and have them drink it; they will immediately recover.
If a person suffers from heart pain, [the same applies].
Recite the mantra over yellow earth twenty-one times and apply it to the painful area;
the ailment will immediately be cured.
If a person suffers from a disease caused by malevolent spirits, [the same applies].
If one recites the mantra over a branch of a pomegranate tree one hundred and eight times and strikes the patient with it, the illness will be cured immediately.
If a person wishes to be loved by a woman,
they should recite the mantra over soil twenty-one times and scatter it upon their own body.
That person should maintain this recollection day after day, without interruption.
If one wishes for a woman to come of her own accord and pay homage,
one should constantly recite the mantra twenty-one times.
He scattered the consecrated ashes over his own body.
That woman then constantly thought of her former lover day and night,
wishing for death so that she might see his face.
If one refuses to leave because they pity someone who is about to die,
and wishes for husband and wife to separate from each other,
take non-glutinous rice and recite the mantra over it twenty-one times.
If one scatters [this substance] over the bodies of a husband and wife, they will immediately depart to a distance and no longer cause each other disturbance or offense.
If there are husbands and wives who hate one another,
and one wishes to bring them into harmony and reunion:
Immediately, one should construct a mandala before the image of the Heavenly King.
Within the mandala, one should draw the figures of a husband and wife.
One should then make offerings of various kinds of food and drink to the image of the Heavenly King.
Then take white mustard seeds and powdered calamus root to form pills—
three hundred and twenty-one in total.
For each pill, recite the mantra once while calling out the names of the husband and wife.
They will immediately become naturally harmonious and free from any further discordant thoughts.
If one wishes to know whether there is an asura cave within the mountains,
one should take white mustard seeds and mix them with one's own blood.
If one recites the mantra one thousand and eight times,
the mountain cave will open by itself;
the asura maiden will then appear like a blazing fire.
Carrying various kinds of incense and flowers, they come to fetch the mantra-practitioner.
If the mantra-practitioner enters this cave,
his lifespan shall last for one great kalpa, and his physical strength will become equal to that of an asura.
Furthermore, like a vajra, it cannot be damaged; when one wishes to depart,
an asura maiden will follow and escort them out,
returning them safely to their original place.
If one seeks to become invisible,
one should take this image of the Heavenly King and smear the ground before a stūpa containing relics with fragrant clay.
One should scatter various kinds of incense and flowers within that mandala. Furthermore,
having completed the offerings of various foods and drinks to the image of the Heavenly King,
one should take wood from a pear tree to fashion a casket.
Take equal parts of guggulu incense and sanakṣīra stone, grind them each into powder,
mix with lacquer-water to form pills,
place them inside a small casket, and set it upon the altar.
The practitioner shall then prepare a pair of new, clean robes,
bathe, and put them on; sitting before an image of the Heavenly King,
they shall fast for one day and recite this mantra one thousand and eight times until it is completed.
Furthermore, there is no need for the manifestation of the three signs;
simply recite it one thousand and eight times,
and then apply it to the eyes, the palms of the hands, the soles of the feet, the chest, and both shoulders.
With palms joined and a focused mind,
contemplate that one's own body is like empty space and devoid of a self.
When this visualization is performed, the practitioner immediately attains the power of invisibility.
One will travel a thousand li per day and all undertakings will be successfully accomplished.
If one seeks to subjugate non-Buddhists or to ensure that one's own body is not burned by fire, [one should practice as follows].
Take one's own blood and mix it with fish blood;
recite the mantra with a mind of wrath twenty-one times and cast it into the fire for the duration of a single meal.
One will not burn one's own body with fire.
If one wishes to subdue non-Buddhists (tīrthikas),
one should form the aforementioned body-seal while maintaining a mind of wrath.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times silently.
All the magical arts of every non-Buddhist (tīrthika) shall be utterly destroyed and none shall succeed.
If one wishes to eliminate all demonic afflictions, such as those caused by vināyakas and other spirits,
one should burn agalloch incense, generate a great wrathful mind,
and recite the mantra with urgency.
Strike the patient with pomegranate seeds;
all ailments caused by ghosts, celestial epidemics, and dragon epidemics will naturally be extinguished.
Furthermore, even if the ritual has not yet been performed:
That patient may sing, laugh, sit, or run about.
Once the powerful spirit has departed,
place water mixed with ashes and flour into a bronze *śarāva* bowl.
Once the pouring out at the gate has been completed,
burn agalloch incense and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times;
thereafter, they will no longer come to cause disturbance.
Furthermore, if one places ashes inside a copper śarāva vessel and places white flowers within the ashes, one may also cure diseases.
Furthermore, if one wishes to purify defilements,
one should construct an altar,
using cow dung to plaster the altar.
The square and circle shall each be two cubits in width and breadth.
Select a young boy, bathe him thoroughly until he is clean,
dress him in new, pure white garments, and have him squat upon the altar.
The youth placed both his hands and feet upon the śāla tree;
as he burned incense of *agaru* and perfumed the youth’s body while reciting the mantra,
the śāla tree immediately shook.
Then that youth himself pointed out the location where the thieves were.
Among all the ritual procedures (*vidhi*) mentioned above, the method of hand gestures (*mudrā*) has not been explained; therefore, the method of seals is now specifically taught.
Hook the two little fingers of both hands together.
Extend the two ring fingers straight upward and outward.
Cross the two middle fingers and the two index fingers behind each other.
The two index fingers are extended straight outward with the palms facing each other’s backs;
this is the *ekavarṇa-mudrā*, which is used universally for the ritual procedures and magical arts described above.
The *Vaiśravaṇamantra-sūtra*, one fascicle.
